item.text: {"role":"story","inspection_scope":"Rough-stage review of all eight ordinary-production shots in both captioned and captionless 360×640 evidence. Assessed ordered decoded frames, native key frames, every supplied consecutive event window, and the complete opening-to-ending progression. Pixel traces were used only to locate holds and motion intervals, not as semantic proof. No MP4 playback or audio listening was performed.","gates":[{"gate":"story","status":"PASS","evidence":"The film presents a complete visible progression: unsafe overwrite endangers the original roof; history catches it; a checkpoint records the restored house; the coral change is compared; the repeated physical test first fails; rollback restores retained parts; the same test passes; the archive closes beneath the restored house."},{"gate":"cause-effect","status":"PASS","evidence":"Major results have painted antecedents: Bot operates controls before mechanisms move, the falling roof trips the history assembly, the checkpoint plate is pressed before storage, the water slug precedes wet-floor deformation, the rollback pull precedes component exchange, and the finale lever precedes the archive display."},{"gate":"focal-hierarchy","status":"PASS","evidence":"Each sentence-level feature becomes the dominant readable form: opposed roofs in shot 1, gold history strip in shot 2, oversized checkpoint plate in shot 3, aligned roof profiles in shot 4, water/floor failure in shot 5, rollback exchange in shot 6, gutter/cup path in shot 7, and the central restored house with flanking state cards in shot 8."},{"gate":"continuity","status":"PASS","evidence":"Persistent roof, facade, floor, water-test and archive identities remain traceable across shots. The failed wet state is retained during rollback, the restored configuration supports the successful repeated test, and the ending returns the teal roof, three-window facade and level dry floor established at the opening."}],"violations":[],"sampling_limits":"The supplied evidence establishes painted ordering and consecutive-frame attachment around declared events, but not sound, narration delivery, or continuous perceived timing between sampled frames. Full-rate pixel deltas are nonsemantic and were not treated as proof of action meaning. Human playback/listening remains required for final approval.","shot_assessments":[{"shot":"shot-01-unsafe-overwrite","gates":[{"gate":"story","status":"PASS","evidence":"The intact teal-roof house visibly becomes an endangered roofless house with the original lifted/released and the coral proposal advancing, giving the metaphor a clear before, action and consequential after."},{"gate":"cause-effect","status":"PASS","evidence":"At 0.667s Bot engages the write control; the coral assembly subsequently advances. At 1.667s Bot contacts the teal roof, later brakes the proposal, releases the original, and operates the late history control at 5.900s."},{"gate":"focal-hierarchy","status":"PASS","evidence":"The large teal original and coral replacement occupy the dominant upper field while Bot’s loaded, then surprised silhouette supports rather than replaces the roof conflict."},{"gate":"continuity","status":"PASS","evidence":"The opening establishes the exact teal roof, three windows and dry level floor later restored. The falling teal roof and braked coral roof carry directly into shot 2."}]},{"shot":"shot-02-history-catches-change","gates":[{"gate":"story","status":"PASS","evidence":"The roofless live house remains visible while the displaced teal roof is caught and carried into a retained bay; the unfolding gold strip supplies a visible record of the removed prior state."},{"gate":"cause-effect","status":"PASS","evidence":"The teal roof depresses the latch at 6.333s, the tongue contacts and assumes the roof at 6.633–6.667s, the strip unfolds, the roof lands at 7.300s, and the terminal linkage reaches the pending rack at 7.433s."},{"gate":"focal-hierarchy","status":"PASS","evidence":"The gold spring, tongue and unfolding strip command the central frame; the house is reduced to context and Bot is appropriately absent."},{"gate":"continuity","status":"PASS","evidence":"The same teal and coral roof cards from shot 1 remain identifiable. The live house stays roofless until the retained teal roof is returned in shot 3."}]},{"shot":"shot-03-save-checkpoint","gates":[{"gate":"story","status":"PASS","evidence":"The teal roof visibly returns before the large gold plate advances over the intact house, takes on its house profile and windows, then retracts into storage; this paints checkpoint creation rather than relying on the caption."},{"gate":"cause-effect","status":"PASS","evidence":"Roof contact and seating occur at 8.233–8.600s; Bot then operates the control at 8.900s; plate registration and pressure occur at 9.267–9.533s; the stamped plate retracts and reaches its archive position by 9.933s."},{"gate":"focal-hierarchy","status":"PASS","evidence":"During capture the oversized yellow checkpoint plate plainly dominates the house and Bot; after storage the intact restored house regains prominence."},{"gate":"continuity","status":"PASS","evidence":"The teal roof returns to the established facade, and the final live house matches the dry opening state before logged work begins. The stored plate remains present for the comparison and rollback chain."}]},{"shot":"shot-04-visible-difference","gates":[{"gate":"story","status":"PASS","evidence":"The shot resolves into a single legible comparison: preserved pitched teal roof on the left and installed flat coral roof on the right over the persistent facade, clearly painting what changed."},{"gate":"cause-effect","status":"PASS","evidence":"The already released rack couples to the roofs, unlocks the teal roof, withdraws it, seats the coral roof, and stops both profiles on a shared display baseline by 10.900s."},{"gate":"focal-hierarchy","status":"PASS","evidence":"The differently shaped teal and coral roof cards are the largest contrasting colored forms, with the gold linkage functioning as explanatory support."},{"gate":"continuity","status":"PASS","evidence":"The teal roof remains the stored before state and the coral roof becomes the live changed state used by the failure test in shot 5."}]},{"shot":"shot-05-rain-test-fails","gates":[{"gate":"story","status":"PASS","evidence":"The test has a clear dry before and wet, sagging after. Bot changes from focused operation to a worried posture as the physical result appears."},{"gate":"cause-effect","status":"PASS","evidence":"Bot grips the test control at 12.067s; the same water slug descends from the reservoir, reaches the coral roof at 12.533s, strikes the window at 12.767s, then impacts and deforms the floor at 12.967s."},{"gate":"focal-hierarchy","status":"PASS","evidence":"The large teal slug creates a readable top-to-bottom path, and the expanding teal wet band on the floor becomes the terminal focal consequence."},{"gate":"continuity","status":"PASS","evidence":"The coral roof installed in shot 4 remains live. The resulting wet sag and worried Bot posture persist into the opening of rollback."}]},{"shot":"shot-06-rollback-restores","gates":[{"gate":"story","status":"PASS","evidence":"The shot visibly exchanges the failed configuration for the retained one: coral roof and damaged floor move toward the failed bay while the teal roof returns to the facade and the cream floor is restored."},{"gate":"cause-effect","status":"PASS","evidence":"Bot’s braced two-handed pull begins at 13.900s before the roof and floor exchanges. Coral transfer, wet-floor transfer, dry-cassette transfer, teal-roof landing and dry-floor landing occur in ordered stages through 16.733s."},{"gate":"focal-hierarchy","status":"PASS","evidence":"Bot’s burdened lean, large rollback tab and crossing component rails form one dominant exchange gesture; the small reset-water mechanism remains subordinate."},{"gate":"continuity","status":"PASS","evidence":"The actual teal roof returns rather than being replaced by a new lookalike. The failed bay retains the coral roof and dark wet-floor state while the live house ends with teal roof and level cream floor."}]},{"shot":"shot-07-restored-test-passes","gates":[{"gate":"story","status":"PASS","evidence":"The same test is repeated on the restored house, but the water travels outward to the side cup while the interior floor stays dry; Bot’s open, happy posture makes the successful result readable."},{"gate":"cause-effect","status":"PASS","evidence":"Bot operates the same rain control at 17.767s; water contacts the teal roof at 18.233s, transfers through the gutter at 18.667s and lands in the exterior cup at 19.067s. Bot later presses the finale control at 20.267s."},{"gate":"focal-hierarchy","status":"PASS","evidence":"The teal water slug, roof edge, gutter and exterior cup form a clean descending path, while the still cream floor supplies the necessary contrast with shot 5."},{"gate":"continuity","status":"PASS","evidence":"The restored teal roof, dry floor and reset water apparatus match the rollback result. Bot exits only after initiating the mechanism that continues into shot 8."}]},{"shot":"shot-08-every-step-reversible","gates":[{"gate":"story","status":"PASS","evidence":"The live restored house is briefly flanked by reduced checkpoint and failed-state cards; the cards then fold away and the house remains in its restored opening identity for the final hold."},{"gate":"cause-effect","status":"PASS","evidence":"The mechanism continues from shot 7, presents both state cards by 21.467s, reverses after the cam contact at 22.867s, folds the failed bay into storage through 23.400–23.767s, and seats the archive beneath the house at 24.100s."},{"gate":"focal-hierarchy","status":"PASS","evidence":"The wide phase makes the central live house primary while the two yellow archive cards operate as large, simplified secondary comparisons. Once they close, the restored house alone commands the ending."},{"gate":"continuity","status":"PASS","evidence":"The final teal pitched roof, three windows and level cream floor visibly match the opening house. The ending therefore pays off the initial endangered state while the preceding display confirms that checkpoint and failed states remain part of the archive."}]}]}
